mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.75% over three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.75% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates expanding manufacturing activity, which boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when INDPRO exceeds its 12-month moving average for six months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and rising inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal income (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both decline for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both PAYEMS and HOUST decline for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate coinciding with a simultaneous fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) over four consecutive months signals a deepening labor market downturn, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) consistently outpace real personal income (PAYEMS) for five consecutive quarters, indicating unsustainable demand fueled by borrowing, which eventually leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days as debt overhang materializes.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > PAYEMS for five consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 exceeds PAYEMS for five consecutive quarters.
